- When sentiment is negative or mixed in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak values.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — dampen forecast slope downward in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., 1.00s clustered), model tends to overestimate — cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high.
- If sentiment is bearish or neutral, model often underestimates — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid under-shoot.
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile — adjust downward by 0.5–1.0% for first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish, model lags — delay forecast drop by 1–3 days and reduce magnitude.
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model often ignores it — add slight upward bias to counteract.
- Forecast should not exceed 2 standard deviations above recent 10-day average unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
